Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Dynasty Petroleum Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Dynasty Petroleum's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Kline, VP of Exploration; Lisa Chen, VP of Marketing; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Dynasty Petroleum delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We made significant strides in our future development plans and resource potential, building a deep inventory across key basins. Our lifting costs per BOE continued their downward trend with aggressive cost reduction initiatives. Production volumes grew across total BOE, oil, and gas, with positive QoQ and YoY changes. Operating expenses per BOE improved through targeted management strategies. Realized prices benefited from our hedging programs. We updated production guidance for next quarter and the full year, considering key influencing factors. Environmental performance remained strong with minimal spills and proactive remediation. Exploration and drilling activities yielded key well results and clear future plans.

I'm particularly pleased with our progress on high-return inventory in the Permian, Eagle Ford, and Gulf of Mexico. We are focused on disciplined capital allocation to drive long-term shareholder value. Further, we are advancing technical initiatives like EOR pilots and digital integrations. We continue to adjust to market dynamics like OPEC+ cuts. We are advancing offshore tie-backs and international farm-ins. We are evaluating emerging plays like Namibia. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize costs and sustainability.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $1.45 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Operating income was $480 million, and net income was $350 million. We generated $320 million in free cash flow and returned $180 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $2.8 billion in debt and $1.2 billion in cash.

Let me dive deeper into some key operational metrics that underpinned these results. Starting with lifting costs per BOE, which is a critical lever for our free cash flow. For the full year to date through Q3 2024, our company-wide lifting costs averaged $9.65 per BOE, reflecting a sharp 20% reduction from $12.10 per BOE in the prior year. In Q3 alone, we hit $8.95 per BOE, down 10% from Q2's $9.95 and 24% year-over-year. This outperforms our guidance and places us in the lower quartile among Permian peers like Pioneer and EOG, and even stacks up well against Gulf operators like Chevron.

Looking at the trend over five years, costs peaked at $14.20 per BOE in 2020 amid low prices and disruptions, then declined to $11.50 in 2021, ticked up slightly to $12.30 in 2022 on inflation, $12.00 in 2023, and now $9.65 year-to-date. This is powered by scale from higher volumes, efficiencies outpacing inflation, and our $500 million annual OpEx program. Permian assets, 65% of production, drove most savings, dropping from $8.40 to $6.70 per BOE, thanks to factory drilling and water recycling at 75% using advanced electrocoagulation tech.

In Eagle Ford, costs fell to $9.30 from $11.60 via pad drilling with 12 wells per pad. Bakken held at $11.00 but AI frac designs target further cuts. Offshore GOM improved dramatically to $18.00 from $24.00 with subsea tie-backs spreading fixed costs. Initiatives include digital twins from Baker Hughes for predictive maintenance, cutting downtime 25%; supply chain locks at 10-15% below spot; water management recycling 18 million barrels; automated rigs boosting efficiency 20%; and divestitures of non-core assets. For 2025, we guide $8.80-$9.30 per BOE.

Next, production volumes. In Q3, total production averaged 285,000 BOE per day, up 2.5% QoQ from 278,000 and 9.6% YoY from 260,000. Oil was 195,000 bbl/d, +1.6% QoQ and +11.4% YoY. Gas equivalent 75,000 BOE/d, -1.3% QoQ but +3.5% YoY. Delaware Basin at 177,000 BOE/d with 118,000 oil bbl/d from new Wolfcamp and Bone Springs wells with 12,500-foot laterals and optimized fracs boosting EURs 15-20%. Midland 71,000 BOE/d, Eagle Ford 34,000 BOE/d. Oil cut at 68%. Q4 guide 290,000-295,000 BOE/d.

Operating expenses per BOE came in at $12.45 for Q3, down 7% QoQ from $13.42 and 18% YoY from $15.18. Full year $13.20, down 22%. Lower quartile vs. peers. Trend: Q4'23 $15.18, Q1'24 $14.65, Q2 $13.85, Q3 $13.42, Q4 guide $12.45. Permian $6.80 LOE, Eagle Ford $16.20, GOM $10.50. Strategies: AI maintenance cutting downtime 30%, G&T renegotiations with take-or-pay, taxes at $1.65, supply efficiencies. 2025 guide $11.50-$12.50.

On realized prices, oil averaged $78.45/bbl vs. WTI $76.20, +$2.25 premium from quality crude. Eagle Ford $79.80, DJ $77.10. Hedged 65% with collars floor $72.50 cap $85, swaps $76.80, adding +$3.10/bbl and $28 million gains. Gas $3.15/MCF vs. HH $3.65, hedged 55% adding +$0.45/MCF and $12 million. Blended $62.30/BOE. 2025 oil 40% hedged at $74 floor.

These metrics position us strongly.

Now, turning to future development plans and resource potential. We're focused on high-return inventory with over 10 years drilling locations, anchored in Permian Tier 1 acreage (70% production), Eagle Ford, and GOM offshore. Permian: 1.2 million net acres, 5.5 BBOE unrisked, PDP 450 MMBOE, total 2P 1.8 BBOE. Wolfcamp C: three rigs Q1 2025 for 120 wells, 10,000-ft laterals, EUR 1.4 MBOE, breakeven <$35, +45,000 BOE/d by 2026, NPV $1.2B. EOR CO2 pilots +15-20% recovery, 800 MMBOE contingent. Eagle Ford 350,000 acres, 2 BBOE, Pearsall 40 wells 2025, IP30 1,800 BOE/d, +20,000 BOE/d. GOM: Green Canyon 50,000 acres, Magnolia 25 MMBOE, Albatross 150 MMBOE, first oil Q4 2025, to 50,000 BOE/d by 2028. Namibia: Mopane-1X 3-5 BBOE, 20% interest. R&D $150M: digital twins, AI seismic. 2025 capex $2.8-3.2B, 350 wells, 12-15% growth to 350,000 BOE/d. 50% FCF payout.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thornton for an operational update.

Mike Thornton: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Wolfcamp A pad online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

For production guidance, we're reaffirming full-year 2024 at 560,000-580,000 BOE/d, 5% YoY growth. Q4 550,000-565,000 BOE/d, oil 340,000-350,000 bbl/d. Driven by 28 Permian rigs, 12,500-ft laterals, Delaware pads IP 12,500 BOE/d EUR 1.4 MBOE. Eagle Ford Catarina 8,000-10,000 BOE/d. Permian 365,000 BOE/d, Guyana 5,000-7,000 net. Offsets: 8-10% declines, 15,000 BOE/d downtime. Risks: weather, regs, gas prices. Upside: bolt-on A&D, EOR pilots. Exit year at 600,000 BOE/d.

Now I will turn it over to Robert Kline for an update on our exploration activities.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin Delaware and are planning to drill 28 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

In Q3, we spudded 28 wells, online 32, 12 rigs. Delaware Wolfcamp A six-well pad: IP30 2,450 BOE/d 72% oil, EUR 1.8-2.2 MBOE. Midland 10-well: 1,950 BOE/d, monster well 3,200 peak. Eagle Ford Pearsall pilot 1,200 BOE/d. GOM Vandal-2 discovery 75 MMBOE. Namibia Mopane-1X promising. Inventory 4,200 locations, DUCs managed. Capex $450M yielded 22,000 BOE/d. Analytics platform boosts EURs. Q4: 30 spuds, 35 online. Future: returns-led, 15-20% growth.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Robert. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our NGL-rich output in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of our premium realizations is significant, supporting robust cash flows.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity. Our electrification targets 75% renewables by 2027, cutting Scope 1 by 30%, with CCUS pilots.

I will now turn the call over to Raj Patel to discuss our technology initiatives.

Raj Patel: Thank you, Elena. We are leveraging technology to improve our operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to optimize our operations. We are also exploring new technologies such as carbon capture and storage. Digital twins, AI seismic, fiber-optics, electric fracs—all driving 20-25% efficiency gains.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production volumes total, oil, gas—QoQ and YoY changes?

Johnathan Hale: Good question, Brian. As Sarah detailed, Q3 volumes were strong at 285,000 BOE/d total, up 2.5% QoQ and 9.6% YoY; oil 195,000 bbl/d +1.6% QoQ +11.4% YoY; gas 75,000 BOE/d -1.3% QoQ +3.5% YoY. Driven by Permian new wells outperforming type curves.

Operator: Our next question comes from Amy Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Amy Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year—factors influencing?

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, Amy. Reaffirming full-year 560k-580k BOE/d. Q4 550k-565k. Positives: D&C ramps, Permian pads, Eagle Ford laterals, Guyana ramp. Risks: downtime, weather, regs, low gas prices. Upside A&D, EOR. Hedged for $80 oil durability.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: Could you please provide more color on lifting costs trends and initiatives?

Mike Thornton: Absolutely, Chris. Q3 $8.95/BOE, down sharply. Trends from $14+ peak to sub-$10 via scale, digital predictive maintenance, supply locks, water recycle 75%, automation, divestitures. Permian led at $6.75. 2025 $8.80-9.30 guide.

Operator: Our next question comes from Dana Wong with BMO. Please go ahead.

Dana Wong: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Robert Kline: Great point, Dana. Outstanding results like Delaware IP 2,450 BOE/d, GOM discovery 75 MMBOE, Namibia potential—de-risk inventory, lower breakevens to $42, enable 15-20% growth, prioritize Tier 1, hedge for returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Evan Ruiz with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Evan Ruiz: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years? [Note: Referring to NGLs/optimized output]

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Evan. Strong Gulf demand for our NGLs, expanding base via pipeline access, premiums persist, supporting FCF as we grow volumes 12-15%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Fiona Grant with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Fiona Grant: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vasquez: Happy to, Fiona. Net-zero 2040, TRIR 0.12. Q3 one minor 12-bbl spill contained, YTD 78 bbls down 48%. Zero Permian spills via ILI inspections 2,800 miles. Incidents down 18%, response 14 min. Remediation $14M with bioremediation, digital twins DAS/DTS detecting 0.1 bbl/d leaks. 98% water recycle, ahead on methane rules. Target zero spills 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Greg Olson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Greg Olson: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Raj Patel: Key ones, Greg: AI frac/predictive maint cutting costs $0.40/BOE, fiber-optics optimizing lift, electric fracs -45% emissions, Palantir analytics +25% EURs, CCUS pilots for blue H2.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
